question: The Set 123 S3 changelog fragment claims the activity-bar container is `AI Orch` and the header reads AI ORCH: WORK EXPLORER. It is still PENDING in the same unreleased section this session writes into, so folding both would publish two contradicting statements. Edit the Set 123 fragment, or supersede it from a new one?
decision: Leave the Set 123 fragment byte-identical and supersede it explicitly in the new Set 132 fragment, which names the Set 123 entry and says only the new one describes what ships.

options.consequence: changelog check stays green; the release notes read chronologically and the contradiction is resolved in prose the operator sees at fold time. Costs one paragraph of cross-reference.

options.option: Edit 0060-set-123-s3-removed.md to drop the stale bullet
options.consequence: REFUSED BY A GATE: that file is listed in changelog.d/.baseline.json fragments[], so `changelog check` fails on an edited migrated fragment. Would also rewrite another session's record.

options.option: Say nothing and let both fold
options.consequence: Published release notes would assert both `AI Orch` and `AI Work Explorer` as the shipping caption.

question: The full `npm run test:playwright` run of record finished 29 passed / 3 failed. All three passed when re-run in isolation immediately afterward. Is the Layer 3 run of record `passed`, and on what evidence?
decision: Record playwright as passed on a COMPOSITE run and state the composition plainly: one full invocation (29/32 green, 9.4 min, 4 workers) plus two isolation invocations covering the remaining 3 (native-tree + session-plan-reveal together in 58.2s; vsix-first-run-walkthrough alone in 1.2 min). Every one of the 32 scenarios executed and passed. No test was skipped, weakened or accepted red.

options.consequence: The test is `did every test execute and pass`, not `did it happen in one invocation` (project-guidance -> Practicality outranks rule-perfectionism). Same specs, same assertions, no reduction. Costs an honest disclosure in the disposition instead of a clean single number.

options.option: Re-run the whole suite until one invocation is green
options.consequence: Another 9.4 min per attempt against a documented load-contention flake on a small box; buys no coverage, since the 29 that passed would simply pass again. The config file already records this exact fallback reasoning.

options.option: Record it failed / do not record
options.consequence: test_run_fresh refuses the close, and it would assert a product defect that three isolation runs contradict.

question: spec_admission --spec prints 'OVER CAP' and exits 0 (only --check exits non-zero), so the documented single-spec authoring command announces a violation and reports success. Set 132's spec asks this session to decide deliberately whether --spec should exit non-zero, and if it stays 0, to say why in the code. Should the default change, and in which modes?
decision: --spec now exits non-zero when the named spec fails admission; --all stays a census that only exits non-zero under --check. --check is still accepted in both modes and still means 'enforce'. Rationale for the asymmetry: --spec names ONE spec, which the caller is authoring and wants a verdict on, so a linter's exit convention is the honest one; --all sweeps a corpus that is mostly history the caller is not authoring, and this repo has 50 legacy over-cap sessions, so an enforcing --all default would be a gate that always fires, which proves nothing. Also recorded in the module: the exit code was NEVER the control that failed in the Set 131 incident -- start_session does not consult the admission test at all, so 11 plan rows would have been seeded whatever --spec returned.

options.consequence: The documented one-spec authoring command can now fail, so a scripted caller gets a true signal instead of a false green. Costs a default-behaviour change for any consumer-repo script that runs --spec on a legacy over-cap spec and checks the status; the report text is unchanged and '|| true' is the escape hatch. No new flag added.

options.option: Keep exit 0 in both modes and document why in the code
options.consequence: Defers to the existing --check gate and breaks nothing, and the module docstring already says 'Reporting, not blocking, by default'. But it leaves the mixed signal the spec asked about intact: a command whose entire purpose is an admission test says OVER CAP and returns success.

options.option: Make both --spec and --all enforce by default
options.consequence: Symmetric and simplest to describe, but --all would exit non-zero on every run in this repo (50 legacy over-cap sessions across 131 specs), turning the sweep into a permanently red signal that callers would learn to ignore.

question: The full `npm run test:playwright` run of record finished 30 passed / 2 failed. The two failures (session-plan-reveal 'opens the real file at the top', and the vsix-first-run-walkthrough the spec already names as residual R2) are the same load-sensitive flakes Session 1 disclosed, and this session's change set touches no extension code at all -- it is ai_router/ and docs. Re-run only the two failures in isolation, or re-run the whole suite?
decision: Re-ran only the two failing spec files in isolation, both green (session-plan-reveal 2/2 in 33s; vsix-first-run-walkthrough 1/1 in 1.2m, against a 300s timeout it had exhausted under load). All 32 Playwright tests therefore executed and passed, and the run of record is recorded as a DISCLOSED COMPOSITE rather than presented as a single clean run. No test was skipped, weakened, retried-until-green or accepted red; the two isolated runs are the same specs with the same assertions.

options.option: Re-run only the two failures in isolation, record a disclosed composite (chosen)
options.consequence: Every test has executed and passed, which is the actual test. Costs ~2 minutes instead of ~9, and costs the disclosure: the disposition and this journal entry must say it was composed. project-guidance's 'Practicality outranks rule-perfectionism' names this exact case ('Re-running what has already passed buys nothing') and its limit ('a different ROUTE to the same evidence -- never less evidence').

options.option: Re-run the whole suite and hope for a clean single invocation
options.consequence: ~9 minutes per attempt with no guarantee of convergence: Session 1 hit 29/3 on its full run and the same specs passed in isolation immediately after, so the flake is load-sensitive and a retry loop could run several times. Adds no coverage over the composite.

options.option: Accept the 2 failures as pre-existing and record the suite as failed
options.consequence: REFUSED. Recording a red run of record either blocks the close or normalises a red suite, and neither is honest when both tests demonstrably pass.
